bihar_raw_news.title: MP Govt releases Bhopal Master Plan 2047 draft | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 27, 2026 MP Govt releases Bhopal Master Plan 2047 draft Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Services The Madhya Pradesh Government has released the draft of the Bhopal Master Plan 2047, setting the stage for public consultation on the proposed land-use framework for the State Capital. The notification was issued on Saturday, days after the Supreme Court considered issues related to commercial activity in Bhopal’s residential areas. The release of the draft plan has raised expectations among traders and property owners facing sealing action, particularly those seeking a change in the designated land use of their properties. However, the Supreme Court’s September 22 order makes it clear that publishing the draft master plan will not, by itself, provide immediate relief from existing sealing orders. The court has permitted the Government to publish the draft plan and invite claims and objections from stakeholders. At the same time, the State Government has assured the court that it will not finalise the proposed master plan without the court’s permission. Consequently, any proposed change in land use contained in the draft cannot automatically make an existing commercial activity in a residential area lawful. The Supreme Court order, which was made public on Friday, deals with Bhopal in paragraphs 17 to 26. During the hearing, the State Government informed the court that the draft of the new master plan had been prepared and sought permission to place it in the public domain for objections and suggestions. The court’s directions mean that the legal status of a property will continue to be determined under the applicable existing master plan and building regulations until the new plan is formally approved. Therefore, a shop or commercial establishment operating in an area currently designated exclusively for residential use could continue to face enforcement action despite a proposal in the draft plan to alter its land-use classification. The order also states that the pendency of a dispute relating to ownership of a property, building or any other matter will not, by itself, prevent authorities from taking action. Where a property is being used contrary to the purpose for which it was allotted or in violation of the approved plan, the competent authorities can proceed in accordance with law. Similarly, construction undertaken without the required approvals can be subjected to sealing or demolition action as prescribed under the applicable legal framework. The court has, however, made a distinction in cases where the existing land-use classification does not clearly specify whether an area is residential or commercial. In such locations, the possibility of mixed use may be considered in accordance with the applicable provisions. Until the issue is resolved, the existing status will remain in place while administrative and documentation processes can continue. The order is particularly significant for traders who had been hoping that the new master plan would immediately resolve the issue of sealing of commercial establishments in residential neighbourhoods. The court’s directions indicate that such relief cannot flow merely from a proposal contained in the draft

Madan Kumar TOI.in Updated On Sep 27, 2026 at 08:17 AM IST CM at Govt Middle School, Ramjichak, under Danapur in Patna district Patna: CM Samrat Choudhary has asked officials to equip govt schools with modern facilities and strengthen their academic environment to prepare students for competitive examinations. Choudhary issued the directions while attending a parent-teacher meeting at Govt Middle School, Ramjichak, under Danapur in Patna district. He reviewed teaching arrangements, attendance, examination results and facilities, and interacted with students, parents and teachers. Advt He directed education department officials to prepare a plan from next year to make computer education compulsory in all govt schools. He suggested one instructor for every two to three schools. He said online teachers and live classes had been provided at model schools at around 700 locations across Bihar. Education minister Mithilesh Tiwari and cooperative minister-cum-Danapur MLA Ram Kripal Yadav were present. bihar_raw_news.title: Meet the 20-year-old whose wastewater innovation earned UNDP recognition
bihar_raw_news.content: Edited By : Anand P Last Updated: 27 September 2026, 09:17 AM IST Share A 20-year-old entrepreneur who moved from Bihar's Madhubani to Mumbai has developed an affordable wastewater treatment system aimed at reducing industrial pollution. Representational Image | Photo: AFP New Delhi: Growing up in the slums of Mumbai after moving from Bihar's Madhubani in search of a better life, Piyush Jha witnessed how wastewater accumulating around homes exposed residents to diseases such as dengue, malaria and typhoid. The experience prompted him to explore a solution to the problem, eventually leading him to develop an affordable wastewater treatment technology that has now earned recognition from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). At just 20, Jha has developed a decentralised, modular wastewater treatment system designed to make wastewater treatment more accessible and affordable, particularly for industries. His innovation has been recognised through UNDP India's entrepreneurship initiative, the 'Youth Co:Lab National Innovation Challenge'. Speaking to PTI on the occasion of World Rivers Day, Jha said his innovation seeks to tackle one of the major sources of pollution in India's water bodies: the discharge of untreated industrial wastewater. He estimated that nearly 18,000 million litres of wastewater are discharged daily in India, of which only 20 to 30 per cent is treated. "We don't require any chemical dosing to treat wastewater, nor do we require heavy civil infrastructure. The current water treatment plants require heavy civil infrastructure just to get started, which is a major concern for manufacturing and processing plants in India," he said. Jha said the technology could indirectly benefit the common person by offering industries a more affordable way to treat wastewater before it is released into the environment. The system is designed for industries such as textiles, leather, food and beverages, distilleries, paper and pulp, and sugar, which generate large volumes of biodegradable waste. The technology uses microorganisms to break down waste while generating electricity in the process, he said. "When small and medium-scale industries get an affordable water treatment solution, they're less likely to discharge toxic wastewater into water bodies. It also helps them financially. An industry may earlier spend Rs 20 lakh on operational costs for water treatment, which our pretreatment solution reduces to Rs 5 to 7 lakh," he told PTI. Industry partnerships and pilot opportunities Jha said his company has already started working with several industry partners interested in the technology. These include Mumbai-based cleantech startup Indra Water, which develops compact, decentralised wastewater treatment systems, and Pune-based sweets and snacks enterprise Chitale Bandhu Mithaiwale. He has also received a conditional purchase order from Dahej Waste Service, a Bharuch-based company in Gujarat that provides commercial and industrial cleaning and waste management services. From a second-hand laptop to a startup Recalling how the idea took shape, Jha said his entrepreneurial journey began during the Covid-19 pandemic, when his mother helped him arrange a second-hand laptop. national_raw_news.content: India has called upon all parties to exercise restraint, de-escalate tensions, ensure protection of civilians, and uninterrupted flow of energy and commerce during ongoing conflicts. Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York last night, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar pointed out that the repercussions of wars are experienced far outside the borders of directly engaged nations. He said hostilities continue to destabilise global security, threatening progress and slowing development far beyond their immediate regions. Dr Jaishankar said India is prepared to do everything possible to help improve the situation, particularly in the areas of food and energy security. Referring to the protracted Russia-Ukraine conflict, the minister said the ongoing war remains a critical international concern and echoed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for an end to hostilities. On the Gulf conflict, Dr Jaishankar said the hostilities are exacerbating an already difficult situation. Turning to maritime security, he said attacks on commercial ships and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea are unacceptable. External Affairs Minister also underscored the imperative of ensuring stable distribution channels for food grains and energy resources. Dr Jaishankar said that India will exercise its right to defend itself against terrorism. He called state-sponsored terrorism with a cross-border purpose a direct challenge to the global order. External Affairs Minister said governments engaged in such practices must be held accountable and the financing of terrorism must be exposed and countered. Dr Jaishankar said the world is witnessing weaponisation of everything, from finance and market access to supply chains and technology. He said countries are responding by reducing risks and diversifying their ties. Dr Jaishankar described a “4F crisis” confronting the Global South – the security of food, fuel, fertiliser and finance. He said India’s growth and public services have improved the prospects of one-sixth of humanity. He cited 600 major Indian development projects in 78 countries, spanning infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture, information technology and capacity building. On artificial intelligence, Dr Jaishankar said, countries should be able to develop their own models and deployment plans in line with national priorities. He said India will make AI part of its partnership agenda with the Global South. External Affairs Minister said that countries should be free to develop artificial intelligence systems that serve their own priorities. He described AI as a tool that can empower people, support economic growth and help address challenges on a large scale.
